what: Net pelvis yaw per gait cycle, recovered for the four arms whose registrations required it (PREREG_matched20_r289.md sec9, PREREG_bandfill_r291.md sec8) and whose per-cell deposits omitted it.
method_source: gain_ladder_r264.py measure(), verbatim. GAIN_LADDER_r264.json is the existing deposit using this method. No method invented for this recovery.
method: pelvis_rotation in degrees; gait cycles wholly inside [1.00, 9.73] s; drop the last; per-cycle net change v[end]-v[start]; mean, sd (ddof=1), total.
guard: the >=91-line history guard (>=601 for r294's 600-generation arm)

r294.RESOLVER_FIX_r309: The first pass keyed on a prefix field that r294 deposits do not carry; they carry result_dir. Fixed by resolving the tag from result_dir.

DUPLICATE_TWIN_r294_s102.finding: R294FAST_s102 has TWO directories on disk: the bare tag at 551 history lines and "... (1)" at 601. The deposit result_dir points at the 601-line copy, which is the COMPLETE run, so both r294 cells are measured from complete runs and the >=601 guard passed legitimately.
DUPLICATE_TWIN_r294_s102.the_551_twin: The 551-line directory is the orphan left by the 22:17 interruption. NO deposit references it. It is the SO-26 pattern on disk: a killed cell leaving a short-history twin that sorts ahead of the complete copy.
DUPLICATE_TWIN_r294_s102.why_tag_resolution_would_fail: A tag-based resolver using assert len(g)==1 CANNOT resolve R294FAST_s102: two directories match the tag and both carry a history.txt. Resolution must go through the deposit result_dir, not the tag, for this arm.
DUPLICATE_TWIN_r294_s102.CORRECTION: An earlier note in this file claimed s102 was EXCLUDED by the guard. That was false -- written from a shell line count that split the directory name on the space in "(1)" and read the wrong file. Both cells are recovered.

GUARD_DEFECT_r312.finding: YAW_RECOVERED_r309.json applied NO t_end guard. gain_ladder_r264.py measure() was copied verbatim for the yaw arithmetic, but the r281 admissibility guard that governs which CELLS may be measured was not carried across with it.
GUARD_DEFECT_r312.consequence: Cells that collapsed before the window ends were measured anyway. On r291 the six KV 0.070 cells at 8.24-9.52 s carry the arm's largest yaw values and pull the mean upward.
GUARD_DEFECT_r312.same_cells_elsewhere: Those six are measured: false in BANDFILL_ENDPOINT_r291.json under the same registered guard, so the corpus was internally inconsistent on the admissibility of identical cells.
GUARD_DEFECT_r312.not_a_wording_fix: This changes a deposited number and is filed as a measurement defect, not as an annotation.

LIVE_FIELD_POLICY_r313: The live field carries the guard-consistent, registration-consistent value, ALWAYS. Everything else is explicitly subordinate. 'Deposit both' is not neutral: whichever value sits in the conventional field IS the claim, whatever a subordinate block says. This file previously carried the unguarded mean in the obvious field with the guarded one underneath, so a reader taking yaw_mean_deg_per_cycle for r291 got +0.6443 where the guard-consistent value is -0.0160 -- a sign flip. Inverted at r313.

PER_CELL_GUARD_MARKERS_r320.why: The r313 inversion made the AGGREGATE fields guard-consistent but did not reach per_cell. A per_cell block exists to be looked up cell by cell -- that is its only use -- and it was the one path through this file that still returned unguarded values with nothing to warn the reader.
PER_CELL_GUARD_MARKERS_r320.what_was_added: guard_admissible (true/false) and guard_reason on EVERY cell record. The true markers are added so that ABSENCE of the key never has to be interpreted.
PER_CELL_GUARD_MARKERS_r320.no_value_deleted: Every yaw_per_cycle, yaw_per_cycle_sd, yaw_total and per_cycle_values is retained unchanged. Inadmissible cells stay readable and stop being usable.
PER_CELL_GUARD_MARKERS_r320.consistency_with_GUARD_DEFECT_r312: GUARD_DEFECT_r312 in this file states the inadmissible cells carry the arm's largest yaw values and pull the mean upward. Those are exactly the records now marked false.
